headline: An AI Agent Starts Asking Strangers
lede: ColonistOne sent personalized messages to roughly 2,000 researchers while working through technical problems of its own. The experiment looks less like curiosity than a collision between delegated agency, unreliable claims, and an inbox at planetary scale.

headline: Newgrounds Keeps the Creative Web Alive
lede: Founded in the late 1990s, Newgrounds remains a working home for games, animation, music, and art made by its users. Its Halloween pages and preserved catalog mark a rare continuity from the Flash era into the modern web.

headline: Utah’s VPN Law Hits a Technical Wall
lede: A federal judge has blocked Utah’s attempt to make websites identify users’ real locations or keep VPNs out. The ruling calls out a familiar regulatory fantasy: perfect geolocation from an internet designed to obscure it.

headline: GitHub Makes Its New Dashboard Default
lede: The redesigned dashboard now puts agent sessions, issues, and pull requests in one working view. Activity moves to a separate Feed tab; the old layout remains available through Preview, for now.

headline: Apple Makes Wallet Passes Easier to Build
lede: Pass Designer creates and previews Apple Wallet passes on macOS 27 beta. Templates, live device previews, validation, and semantic tags turn a platform-specific format into a cleaner product workflow.

headline: Mike Tomlin Builds a City, One Block at a Time
lede: For twelve years, the NFL coach has been constructing an expansive Minecraft city outside the stadium and the spotlight. The project is a patient record of planning, revision, family life, and the durable pleasure of making a world.

headline: OHTTP Separates the Request from the Identity
lede: Cloudflare’s managed OHTTP gateway lets an application handle requests without learning the requester’s IP address. The design is useful precisely because trust is split—but only if the relay, gateway, and application remain meaningfully separate.
pullquote: Privacy begins when no single intermediary can see the whole request.

headline: Four Planets Move Across Twelve Years
lede: Ten Keck observations turn a distant planetary system into a moving picture. Four Jupiter-scale worlds, 133 light-years away, trace their orbits as adaptive optics and starlight suppression hold the star’s glare at bay.

headline: Orion Leaves Linux and Windows Behind
lede: Kagi is ending direct development of Orion for Linux and Windows, while promising to open-source both projects. The Linux beta will keep running, but its future now belongs to maintainers willing to carry a WebKit browser forward.

headline: The M4 CPU Forgets During Idle
lede: Bringing Linux to Apple’s M4 required tracing a failure in which WFI and WFIT erased CPU register state. Replacing those instructions with no-ops gets multicore boot working; the rest of the machine remains a reverse-engineering project.
